events.title: New York City Subway Opens
events.description: The first underground line of the New York City Subway, operated by the Interborough Rapid Transit Company (IRT), opened to the public, running from City Hall north to 145th Street in Manhattan.
events.significance: It launched what became one of the largest and busiest rapid transit systems in the world, shaping the growth and daily life of New York City.

events.title: Black Saturday During the Cuban Missile Crisis
events.description: A U.S. U-2 reconnaissance plane piloted by Major Rudolf Anderson was shot down over Cuba by a Soviet surface-to-air missile, and the crisis reached its most dangerous point. Soviet submarine B-59 also came close to launching a nuclear torpedo after being targeted by U.S. depth charges.
events.significance: This was the tensest day of the closest moment the world has come to nuclear war. Restraint by leaders and individuals, and back-channel diplomacy, helped lead to a resolution the following day.

events.title: Birth of Theodore Roosevelt
events.description: Theodore Roosevelt was born in New York City. He became the 26th President of the United States, serving from 1901 to 1909 after the assassination of William McKinley.
events.significance: Roosevelt championed progressive reforms, trust-busting, and conservation, protecting millions of acres of public land, and he won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1906 for mediating the end of the Russo-Japanese War.

events.title: Turkmenistan Declares Independence from the Soviet Union
events.description: Turkmenistan declared independence from the Soviet Union amid the collapse of the USSR, with its Supreme Soviet adopting the declaration after a referendum endorsed independence.
events.significance: It was among the series of independence declarations that ended the Soviet Union, and the date is now celebrated as Independence Day in Turkmenistan.
